why: A (universes 0): for N a slice submanifold of a Euclidean V with the induced Levi-Civita connection, DX/dt := P_{c(t)} X'(t), any curve c and fields X, Y along c (tangent at every t) differentiable at t: d/dt⟨X, Y⟩ = ⟨DX/dt, Y⟩ + ⟨X, DY/dt⟩. B: Lemma 8.3 on an abstract manifold with a smooth Riemannian metric (Mathlib RiemannianBundle) and ANY Mathlib connection compatible in Milnor's sense (parallel fields have constant inner products), for any operation D satisfying Milnor's axioms (a)-(c) and smooth fields V, W. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: A concerns only the induced connection of an embedded submanifold, where the lemma is the product rule in V plus ⟨P X', Y⟩ = ⟨X', Y⟩; B needs, for an arbitrary compatible connection, Lemma 8.2 on an abstract manifold (parallel orthonormal frames), uniqueness of D (Lemma 8.1), and smoothness of the frame coefficients — none in the project or Mathlib (the project's parallel transport is only for embedded N). Even via Whitney embedding, B's connection is not the induced one. B ⇒ A holds only vacuously (A re-proved in 4 lines from inner_tanProj_of_mem, inner_tanProj_left, tanProj_eq_self); B also does not cover A's merely-differentiable-at-t fields or non-smooth c.
